summary: Dickinson's Landing Lighthouse marked the Cornwall Canal's upper entrance from 1865 and was rebuilt in 1891; the tower now stands at Upper Canada Village.

structures.note: Moved from Dickinson's Landing to Upper Canada Village; date of move not in our sources

access.note: At Upper Canada Village; entry to the park is paid. The lighthouse is viewed from across a short canal; visitors cannot walk right up to it (Lighthouse Friends). Grounds open, tower closed.

events.note: Cornwall Canal Lighthouse erected at the upper entrance of the canal, fixed white light (Lighthouse Friends); station established 1865 (Rowlett)
Light transferred from the Department of Railways and Canals to the Department of Marine on 1 July 1890
Old tower replaced by a new square wooden tower, contract by Wm. H. Miller of Moulinette, $253; total cost $326.33, completed 5 October 1891
Characteristic changed from fixed white to fixed
Control passed to the Canal Administration of the Department of Transport

notes_for_editor: Moderate-thin station: two real sources for the light itself (Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett) plus a community essay for the village, and three Department keeper lists. Chapters used: place, building, keepers, after the keepers, today; there are no storms, wrecks or rescues sourced for this light. MATCHED BY POSITION: the 'Cornwall Canal, upper entrance' station name on the keeper-list pages (fact-checker, 2026-10-28, page images: 1902v36i9p21_0083 scan 255 printed 143; 1904v38i8p21_0209 scan 225 printed 211; 1905v39i9p21_0266 scan 168 printed 154; the researcher's scan numbers were each one low). Each Stoneburner row was viewed: 1901 and 1903 lists give 'Cornwall Canal, upper entrance'; the 1904 list gives 'Dickinson Landing'. All three give his appointment as 12 April 1890, which the story now states against Lighthouse Friends' 1881. The essay gives 1957 in one passage and 1958 as the flood year; the story uses only the 1958 quotation. LIGHTHOUSE FRIENDS' 1891 QUOTATIONS: the 1891 Annual Report of the Department of Marine is not in our corpus (marine_ca covers 1900 to 1924); the 1891 figures (contract to Miller, $253, $326.33, 5 October 1891, 'very much out of repair') rest on Lighthouse Friends' quotation and were not checked against the 1891 report. CANAL DISAGREEMENTS left in the story: opening 1843 (LF) vs 1842 (essay); six locks (LF) vs seven (essay). The 1865 date rests on Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett; LF cites no primary source for it. MOVE DATE: none of the sources read gives the year the lighthouse was moved to Upper Canada Village. A community post by the Historical Society of South Dundas (Facebook) says 1958; it is not a source we can cite, so the story does not give it. Record corrections: agency truncated ('St'); the 1950 deactivation year is not supported by the sources read here.
